values.label: Tidal volume
values.location: 22.3, Respiratory Volumes and Capacities; Figure 22.18 (current web edition)
values.where: 22.3, Respiratory Volumes and Capacities; Figure 22.18 (current web edition)
values.excerpt: Tidal volume (TV) is the amount of air that normally enters the lungs during quiet breathing, which is about 500 milliliters.
values.note: A typical teaching value, not a universal reference.

values.label: Residual volume
values.location: Table 30.1, Lung Volumes and Capacities (Avg Adult Male)
values.where: Table 30.1, Lung Volumes and Capacities (Avg Adult Male)
values.excerpt: Air left in the lungs after a forced exhalation
values.note: Table 30.1 lists 1.2 under Volume (liters): 1.2 L × 1000 = 1200 mL. Average adult male teaching value, not a universal reference range.

values.label: Functional residual capacity
values.location: Table 30.1, Lung Volumes and Capacities (Avg Adult Male)
values.where: Table 30.1, Lung Volumes and Capacities (Avg Adult Male)
values.excerpt: Volume of air remaining after a normal exhalation
values.note: Table 30.1 lists 2.4 under Volume (liters): 2.4 L × 1000 = 2400 mL. Average adult male teaching value, not a universal reference range.

values.label: Total lung capacity
values.location: 22.3, Respiratory Volumes and Capacities; Figure 22.18 (current web edition)
values.where: 22.3, Respiratory Volumes and Capacities; Figure 22.18 (current web edition)
values.excerpt: about 6000 mL air for males, and about 4200 mL for females.
values.note: Approximate young adult, female–male; real reference values depend on age, sex and height.

values.label: Vital capacity
values.location: 22.3, Respiratory Volumes and Capacities; Figure 22.18 (current web edition)
values.where: 22.3, Respiratory Volumes and Capacities; Figure 22.18 (current web edition)
values.note: Approximate adult range; real reference values depend on age, sex and height.

values.label: Lung compliance
values.excerpt: Normally, the total compliance of both lungs in an adult is approximately 200 mL/cm H₂O.
values.note: Combined compliance of both lungs. The source is archived; this is a physiology teaching value.

values.label: FEV1/FVC
values.location: Limits of normal; Interpretation of spirometry
values.where: Limits of normal; Interpretation of spirometry
values.excerpt: 5th percentile (corresponding to a z score of -1.645)
values.note: LLN = lower limit of normal, z = −1.645. A z-score describes distance from predicted in standard deviations. Interpret with history and test quality; this is not a diagnosis.

values.label: Bronchodilator response
values.location: Bronchodilator responsiveness testing, Box 1: Determination of a bronchodilator response; accepted manuscript PDF page 12
values.where: Bronchodilator responsiveness testing, Box 1: Determination of a bronchodilator response; accepted manuscript PDF page 12
values.excerpt: A change of >10% is considered a significant BDR response.
values.note: Change in FEV1 or FVC divided by its predicted value; not percent change from baseline. Response alone does not diagnose asthma or exclude COPD. This is a decision threshold, not a typical normal response; no baseline response is assigned. Verbatim wording from Box 1 of the accepted manuscript of this standard.

states.label: Normal
states.mechanism: Reference pattern: air moves freely and lung stretch is balanced.
states.summary: Reference pattern: air moves freely and lung stretch is balanced.
